text:
Filip Chytil was out of the lineup for about two weeks between late October and mid-November, and his return came with a bang: two goals in Vegas on Nov. 15, the night Vancouver ended a seven-game losing streak, per NDTV Sports, and a wraparound the next night that Daniel Wagner of Pass it to Bulis called "What a goal." He played only 12 games last season, so every stretch in the lineup counts.

Vancouver is leaning on him, at 19.5 minutes a night, and he has 5 points (3 goals) in 11 games. His finishing is in line with his chances (3 goals on 2.55 expected goals, the quality of chances).

The five-on-five picture is rough. With Chytil on the ice, the Canucks have taken just 27% of the expected goals and 37% of shot attempts, and they have still scored 6.12 more goals than those chances deserve. Evolving-Hockey notes his teammates rank in the bottom 7%, which drags those numbers down, but that gap between chances and goals is the thing to watch. The goals are nice; the shot share is the story.
